significance: A thirteenth-century Hindu-Buddhist temple of the Singhasari kingdom about 22 kilometres from Malang, commemorating King Vishnuvardhana deified as Shiva in the form of the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara; the name Adityawarman appears on a Manjushri image of 1343 found here. The Nagarakretagama of the fourteenth century calls it majestic and records a visit by King Hayam Wuruk on royal progress. Its bas-reliefs run through four narrative cycles, read anticlockwise in the prasawya manner.
story: Among the reliefs are scenes of King Angling Dharma, remembered as able to understand the speech of animals, alongside Tantri fables that teach moral lessons through animal characters.
